raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, Qwen3.8 QSA decode and speculative verify run the sparse attention as two passes:
1. a Triton gather copies each row's selected KV (up to 2051 positions) into packed scratch;
2. a Triton decode runs one program per (row, KV head).

At decode batch sizes that is an extra round trip through the selected KV, and most of the GPU sits idle. At 32k context with MTP on one MI355X, QSA attention takes about 9.4% of decode GPU time, roughly 120 µs per layer call.

AITER now has a fused FlyDSL kernel for gfx950: `aiter.ops.flydsl.qsa_sparse_decode` [(AITER PR](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6670)). It reads the selected KV straight from the pool through `req_to_token` and splits each row's selection across CTAs. This PR serves QSA decode and verify with it.

## Modifications

- `QwenSparseAttnBackend.forward_decode` → `_forward_paged_attention` takes the fused kernel first on HIP when `can_use_flydsl_qsa_sparse_decode` accepts the operands: gfx950, bf16 q, bf16 or fp8 KV, head_dim 256, GQA group ≤ 16. That covers decode, target verify and draft extend, since each query row is its own length-one query. Everything else falls through to the existing path unchanged.
- **Split count:** `recommended_num_splits` sets the KV split count per batch size, so it is fixed for each captured CUDA graph.
- **Workspace:** sized once at the captured maximum with `workspace_partials`, because graphs keep raw pointers to it. A larger eager batch gets a per-call workspace.
- **Switch:** `SGLANG_ENABLE_QSA_FLYDSL_DECODE` (default on) turns the path off. An AITER build without the module logs a warning and uses the existing path.
- Imports `envs` in `qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py`.
- **Tests:**
  - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/qsa/test_qsa_flydsl_decode.py` checks that the backend gives the kernel the same rows, lengths and per-row request map as the Triton fallback, and that the outputs match.
  - Kernel correctness tests live in AITER (`op_tests/test_flydsl_qsa_sparse_decode.py`).
  - `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_qsa_sparse_decode.py` compares the two paths.

Requires AITER with `aiter.ops.flydsl.qsa_sparse_decode`. No recommended-deployment flags change, so the cookbook page is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K through the chat API: greedy, thinking off, final number scored, 1024 max tokens, MTP on with real acceptance.
- **Short:** 500 questions, 88-token prompts.
- **Long:** 48 questions, each preceded by 120 solved problems (~23k-token prompts), so decode selects 2051 of ~23k positions.

Accept length is total completion tokens ÷ total verify steps, from each response's `spec_tokens_details`.

| MI355X, TP1, MTP 3/1/4 | Triton (flag off) | FlyDSL (this PR) |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K short (500) | 95.2% | 96.0% |
| GSM8K long, ~23k ctx (48) | 95.8% | 97.9% |
| MTP accept length, short | 3.503 | 3.506 |
| MTP accept length, long | 3.394 | 3.441 |

Repeated baseline runs vary by about 1 point on short GSM8K, so the accuracy differences are within noise.

At the kernel level, against an fp64 reference at Qwen3.8 TP1 shapes (Hq=24, Hkv=2, top-k 2051), the fused kernel is more accurate than the Triton path it replaces:
- relative L2 error 1.7e-3 vs 4–6e-3;
- 3–5× lower max error with a peaked softmax.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Setup:**
- 1× MI355X: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Quark MXFP4 (PLE FP8), TP1, `--attention-backend aiter --page-size 64`, MTP NEXTN 3/1/4, `--max-running-requests 16`.
- The only difference between the two arms is `SGLANG_ENABLE_QSA_FLYDSL_DECODE` = 0 / 1.
- Perf runs use simulated MTP acceptance (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.32`), so both arms do identical verify work; accept length is 2.32 in both.

**End to end:** ISL 32768 / OSL 32768, 24 prompts at concurrency 8, 8 warmup requests (`sglang.benchmark.serving`, random dataset).

| | Triton | FlyDSL | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 977.2 | 1075.0 | **+10.0%** |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 8.06 | 7.31 | **−9.3%** |
| P99 TPOT (ms) | 8.20 | 7.43 | −9.4% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 4275 | 4388 | +2.6% |
| Mean E2E latency (s) | 268.3 | 243.8 | −9.1% |
| Benchmark duration (s) | 804.8 | 731.6 | −9.1% |

TTFT is prefill, which this PR does not touch; the difference is run-to-run noise.

**Decode profile:** 40 decode steps at full batch, 8 requests at 32k context, MTP.

| | Triton | FlyDSL |
|---|---:|---:|
| QSA attention GPU time | 72.0 ms (9.4%) | 20.0 ms (2.8%) |
| per QSA call (600 calls) | 120.0 µs | 33.3 µs |
| total GPU kernel time | 767.7 ms | 705.2 ms (−8.1%) |

Triton per call: `_sparse_gqa_chunk_prefill` 71.8 µs + `_compact_kv` 39.4 µs + `_fa2_valid_counts` 4.4 µs + `_fa2_prefix_sum` 4.4 µs. FlyDSL per call: `sparse_decode_attn_kernel` 28.9 µs + `sparse_decode_reduce_kernel` 4.4 µs.

**Kernel benchmark:** `bench_qsa_sparse_decode.py`, top-k 2051, cold cache, CUDA graph.

| Hkv, group | batch | FlyDSL (µs) | Triton gather + decode (µs) | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2, 12 (TP1) | 1 | 16.6 | 89.6 | 5.4× |
| 2, 12 | 4 | 17.2 | 97.6 | 5.7× |
| 2, 12 | 16 | 25.3 | 112.4 | 4.4× |
| 2, 12 | 64 | 59.7 | 202.6 | 3.4× |
| 2, 12 | 128 | 100.9 | 344.4 | 3.4× |

+"""Benchmark: QSA sparse decode attention on gfx950.
+
+``fused_flydsl`` (``aiter.ops.flydsl.qsa_sparse_decode``) reads the selected KV
+straight from the pool and splits each row across CTAs. ``gather_triton`` is the ROCm path it replaces in
+``QwenSparseAttnBackend._forward_paged_attention``: a Triton gather into packed
+scratch, then ``sparse_gqa_packed_decode_triton`` with one program per row and
+KV head.
+
+Cold cache: each captured call reads a different random slice of a pool that is
+several times larger than MI355X's 256 MB last-level cache.
+"""
+
+import itertools
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.benchmark import marker
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=120, stage="jit-kernel-benchmark", runner_config="amd")
+
+DIM = 256
+TOPK = 2051  # Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 512 compressed blocks x ratio 4 + 3
+MAX_CTX = 8192
+POOL_SLOTS = 1 << 21  # 2 GiB of bf16 K+V at Hkv=2
+# Touch at least 4x the last-level cache across the rotated calls.
+COLD_BYTES = 4 << 30
+
+
+def _fused_flydsl(q, k, v, req_to_token, row_req, indices, seq_lens, splits, ws):
+    from aiter.ops.flydsl.qsa_sparse_decode import flydsl_qsa_sparse_decode
+
+    return flydsl_qsa_sparse_decode(
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        req_to_token,
+        row_req,
+        indices,
+        seq_lens,
+        DIM**-0.5,
+        num_splits=splits,
+        workspace=ws,
+    )
+
+
+def _gather_triton(q, k, v, req_to_token, row_req, indices, seq_lens, splits, ws):
+    from sglang.srt.layers.attention.qsa.sparse_attn import (
+        qwen_sparse_fa2_cu_seqlens_triton,
+        qwen_sparse_kv_extraction_compact_triton,
+        sparse_gqa_packed_decode_triton,
+    )
+
+    batch, topk = indices.shape
+    counts = torch.empty(batch, dtype=torch.int32, device=q.device)
+    cu_k = torch.empty(batch + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=q.device)
+    qwen_sparse_fa2_cu_seqlens_triton(seq_lens, indices, counts, cu_k, batch, topk)
+    packed_k = torch.empty(
+        batch * topk, k.shape[1], DIM, dtype=q.dtype, device=q.device
+    )
+    packed_v = torch.empty_like(packed_k)
+    qwen_sparse_kv_extraction_compact_triton(
+        k,
+        v,
+        req_to_token,
+        row_req,
+        indices,
+        seq_lens,
+        cu_k,
+        packed_k,
+        packed_v,
+        batch,
+        topk,
+    )
+    relative = torch.arange(topk, dtype=torch.int32, device=q.device).expand(batch, -1)
+    relative = relative.masked_fill(relative >= counts[:, None], -1).contiguous()
+    cu_q = torch.arange(batch + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=q.device)
+    return sparse_gqa_packed_decode_triton(
+        q, packed_k, packed_v, relative, cu_q, cu_k, counts, DIM**-0.5
+    )
+
+
+FN_MAP = {"fused_flydsl": _fused_flydsl, "gather_triton": _gather_triton}
+
+
+@marker.parametrize(
+    "num_kv_heads,group", [(2, 12), (1, 3)], [(2, 12)]
+)  # TP1 and the cookbook's TP8 per-rank shape
+@marker.parametrize("batch", [1, 4, 16, 64, 128], [1, 64])
+@marker.benchmark("impl", ["fused_flydsl", "gather_triton"])
+def benchmark(num_kv_heads: int, group: int, batch: int, impl: str):
+    from aiter.ops.flydsl.qsa_sparse_decode import recommended_num_splits
+
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+    q = torch.randn(batch, num_kv_heads * group, DIM, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+    q = q.bfloat16()
+    k = torch.randn(POOL_SLOTS, num_kv_heads, DIM, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+    k = k.bfloat16()
+    v = torch.randn_like(k)
+    touched = batch * num_kv_heads * TOPK * DIM * 2 * 2
+    rotations = max(2, min(256, -(-COLD_BYTES // touched)))
+    req_to_token = torch.randint(
+        1,
+        POOL_SLOTS,
+        (rotations * batch, MAX_CTX),
+        generator=gen,
+        device="cuda",
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+    )
+    # Each rotation maps the same positions through different requests' slots.
+    row_reqs = [
+        torch.arange(r * batch, (r + 1) * batch, device="cuda")
+        for r in range(rotations)
+    ]
+    seq_lens = torch.full((batch,), MAX_CTX, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    indices = torch.stack(
+        [
+            torch.randperm(MAX_CTX, generator=gen, device="cuda")[:TOPK].sort().values
+            for _ in range(batch)
+        ]
+    ).int()
+    splits = recommended_num_splits(batch, num_kv_heads, TOPK, q.device)
+    partials = batch * num_kv_heads * group * splits
+    workspace = (
+        torch.empty(partials, device="cuda"),
+        torch.empty(partials, device="cuda"),
+        torch.empty(partials * DIM, device="cuda"),
+    )
+    fn = FN_MAP[impl]
+    rotation = itertools.cycle(row_reqs)
+
+    def call():
+        row_req = next(rotation)
+        return fn(q, k, v, req_to_token, row_req, indices, seq_lens, splits, workspace)
+
+    return marker.do_bench(
+        call,
+        graph_clone_args=None,
+        memory_args=None,
+        memory_output=None,
+        extra_memory_footprint=touched,
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    benchmark.run()

+"""QwenSparseAttnBackend wiring of AITER's fused FlyDSL QSA sparse decode (gfx950).
+
+Kernel correctness is covered in AITER
+(``op_tests/test_flydsl_qsa_sparse_decode.py``); this checks that the
+backend hands the kernel the same operands as the Triton fallback.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+pytest.importorskip("flydsl")
+qsa_flydsl = pytest.importorskip("aiter.ops.flydsl.qsa_sparse_decode")
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=60, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")
+
+
+def _gfx950_available() -> bool:
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.version.hip is None:
+        return False
+    probe = torch.empty(1, 1, 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    return qsa_flydsl.can_use_flydsl_qsa_sparse_decode(probe, probe, probe)
+
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not _gfx950_available(), reason="gfx950 FlyDSL required"
+)
+
+_DIM = 256
+# Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 512 compressed blocks x ratio 4 + 3.
+_TOPK = 2051
+_MAX_CTX = 8192
+
+
+def _make_inputs(rows, num_kv_heads, group, num_slots=40000, seed=0):
+    """Random decode batch: sorted valid prefixes of varying length, then ``-1``
+    padding and one masked entry at ``seq_len``; row 0 selects nothing."""
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    q = torch.randn(rows, num_kv_heads * group, _DIM, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+    k = torch.randn(num_slots, num_kv_heads, _DIM, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+    v = torch.randn(num_slots, num_kv_heads, _DIM, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+    req_to_token = torch.randint(
+        1,
+        num_slots,
+        (rows + 4, _MAX_CTX),
+        generator=gen,
+        device="cuda",
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+    )
+    row_req = torch.randperm(rows + 4, generator=gen, device="cuda")[:rows]
+    seq_lens = torch.randint(
+        _TOPK // 2, _MAX_CTX, (rows,), generator=gen, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    indices = torch.full((rows, _TOPK), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    for r in range(rows):
+        seq_len = int(seq_lens[r])
+        count = 0 if (r == 0 and rows > 1) else (r * 977) % _TOPK + 1
+        count = min(count, seq_len)
+        picked = torch.randperm(seq_len, generator=gen, device="cuda")[:count]
+        indices[r, :count] = picked.sort().values.int()
+        if count < _TOPK:
+            indices[r, count] = seq_len
+    return (
+        q.bfloat16(),
+        k.bfloat16(),
+        v.bfloat16(),
+        req_to_token,
+        row_req,
+        indices,
+        seq_lens,
+    )
+
+
+def test_backend_decode_matches_triton_fallback(monkeypatch):
+    """The backend must hand the kernel the same rows, lengths and request map
+    the Triton fallback uses, including requests resolved per row."""
+    from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+    from sglang.srt.layers.attention import qwen_sparse_attn_backend as qsa_module
+
+    rows, num_kv_heads, group = 6, 2, 12
+    q, k, v, req_to_token, row_req, indices, seq_lens = _make_inputs(
+        rows, num_kv_heads, group
+    )
+    backend = qsa_module.QwenSparseAttnBackend.__new__(qsa_module.QwenSparseAttnBackend)
+    backend.token_to_kv_pool = SimpleNamespace(
+        get_key_buffer=lambda layer_id: k, get_value_buffer=lambda layer_id: v
+    )
+    backend.req_to_token_pool = SimpleNamespace(req_to_token=req_to_token)
+    backend.qsa_profile = None
+    backend._cuda_graph_max_tokens = 0
+    backend._fa2_scratch = {}
+    backend._flydsl_decode_workspace = None
+    metadata = SimpleNamespace(
+        is_cuda_graph=False, sequence_lengths=seq_lens, row_req_pool_indices=row_req
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(backend, "_resolve_metadata", lambda forward_batch: metadata)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(qsa_module, "_resolve_trtllm_sparse_decode", lambda: None)
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(layer_id=0, scaling=_DIM**-0.5)
+    # Per-row requests win over the batch's; poison the batch's to prove it.
+    forward_batch = SimpleNamespace(req_pool_indices=torch.zeros_like(row_req))
+
+    outputs = {}
+    for enabled in (False, True):
+        qsa_module._resolve_flydsl_sparse_decode.cache_clear()
+        with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_QSA_FLYDSL_DECODE.override(enabled):
+            outputs[enabled] = backend._forward_paged_attention(
+                q, layer, forward_batch, indices
+            )
+    qsa_module._resolve_flydsl_sparse_decode.cache_clear()
+    assert backend._flydsl_decode_workspace is not None, "fused path did not run"
+    # Row 0 selects nothing; only the fused kernel defines that output (zeros).
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        outputs[True][1:].float(), outputs[False][1:].float(), atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import sys
+
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
